note: Frozen cross-language vectors for the pairing short-authentication code (S6, review 2026-08-07). THE WHOLE POINT of this code is that two screens show the SAME six digits for the same pairing link: the guardian's QR screen in MyCharter (TypeScript, src/domain/pairingSas.ts), the ward's landing page at /pair (hand-written JS inside public/pair/index.html, which has no bundler and so cannot import the module), and the ward's own Charter app (Kotlin, PairingSas.kt) — which is the screen that actually renders in the verified App-Link flow, and therefore the one that matters. Three implementations exist because these three runtimes cannot share code. If they ever disagree, a family sees two different codes for the same link, concludes the check is broken, and taps through it — which is worse than never having shown a code at all. So every implementation is pinned to THIS file.
derivation: code = decimal(first 3 bytes of SHA-256("charter-pair-sas:v1:" + lowercase(pubkeyHex) + ":" + token), big-endian) mod 1000000, zero-padded to 6 digits, rendered as "NNN NNN".
notOnTheWire: This value is never transmitted. Both sides derive it independently from the (guardian pubkey, one-time token) they already hold, which is exactly what makes comparing them out loud meaningful. It is a comparison code, not a secret: the modulo bias on the largest residues is irrelevant and must not be 'fixed' in a way that breaks agreement.

vectors.name: a different guardian, same token - THE attack this exists for
same guardian, a fresh token - a code seen once is not replayable
an upper-case pubkey normalizes to the same code
a code with leading zeros - padding must not be dropped

npubNote: The npub shown beside the code, so the two screens can also be compared character for character when six digits are not enough. NIP-19 bech32 of the same x-only pubkey. Kotlin and the /pair page each hand-roll bech32; MyCharter uses nostr-tools.
